title: IRQs
body:
IRQ stands for *Interrupt Request*.

Careful with this one: the *service* belongs to [[ISRs|ISR]], not to IRQ. It is easy to
cross the two because they always show up together.

| | Stands for | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **IRQ** | Interrupt **Request** | The *signal*. Hardware raising its hand to say it needs attention. |
| **ISR** | Interrupt **Service** Routine | The *code*. What the CPU runs in response. |

So the order of events is: a device raises an IRQ → the [[PIC]] decides whether it wins on
priority ([[IPL]], [[Interrupt Mask]]) → the [[Vector Tables|vector table]] says which
[[ISRs|ISR]] to jump to → the ISR runs, saves and restores context, and the interrupted
program never finds out.

**Sources of IRQs**
- Keyboard interrupts
- Mouse movement
- Monitors (VBL, see [[VBL ISR]])

See [[Interrupt Driven I-O]] for the whole mechanism, and [[Concurrency]] for why an ISR
touching a shared variable is a problem.
